candidates.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
candidates.why: The presence of neoplastic squamous cells and malignant features supports this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Sebaceous carcinoma
support_spans: Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor
contradict_spans: Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor
candidates.why: The absence of specific sebaceous markers makes this diagnosis less likely.

candidates.why: The presence of squamous cells and the specific growth pattern contradict this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
candidates.why: The presence of malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, along with mitotic figures, supports this diagnosis.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked due to the lesion's initial appearance as a benign growth.

candidates.name: Keratoacanthoma
support_spans: Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
contradict_spans: Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
candidates.why: The lesion's appearance and the presence of pseudohorn cysts could suggest keratoacanthoma, but the malignant features indicate a more aggressive process.
candidates.protected_reason: Keratoacanthoma is a rare and sometimes controversial diagnosis that may be underconsidered in the differential diagnosis.

candidates.name: Clear cell squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: Central areas of clear cell change were periodic acid–Schiff positive and diastase sensitive
candidates.why: The presence of clear cell changes with specific staining patterns suggests a variant of squamous cell carcinoma.
candidates.protected_reason: This variant may be easily missed due to its rarity and the need for specific histopathological stains to confirm the diagnosis.
